export const meta = {
  name: 'larger-model-evaluation',
  description: 'Haiku and Sonnet answer the same oracle-free evaluation prompts as the small models, five batches each',
  phases: [{ title: 'Answer' }],
}
const dir = '<repo>/evaluation/registry/agent-models'
const task = (model, batch) => `You are the model under evaluation in a scientific comparison of language models. Read ONLY the file ${dir}/prompts-${batch}.json. It has "templates" (for each condition, a chat: a system message, optionally solved example turns, and a final user turn containing {{STATEMENT}}) and "items" (key, condition, statement).

For EACH item, imagine a fresh conversation consisting of that condition's template with {{STATEMENT}} replaced by the item's statement, and write the reply you, as the assistant, would give to the final user turn, following the system message exactly (for example: one javascript code block; one sop code block; one json code block; or a one-sentence direct answer). Answer each item independently of the others.

Rules, which are part of the scientific protocol:
- Do not execute, test, or run any code, and do not use any tool other than reading that one input file and writing your output file. Compute nothing with tools; write the reply as you would in a normal conversation.
- Do not read any other file or directory, and do not use git or the web.
- Do not skip items and do not abbreviate replies; every key must appear exactly once.

Write your replies to ${dir}/answers-${model}-${batch}.jsonl, one JSON object per line: {"key": "<the item key>", "reply": "<your full reply text>"}. Append in groups of about 20 items so partial work is kept. When done, reply with the number of items written.`
const jobs = []
for (const model of ['haiku', 'sonnet']) for (const batch of ['b1', 'b2', 'b3', 'b4', 'b5']) jobs.push({ model, batch })
const results = await parallel(jobs.map(j => () => agent(task(j.model, j.batch), { label: `${j.model}-${j.batch}`, phase: 'Answer', model: j.model })))
return results.map((r, i) => ({ job: `${jobs[i].model}-${jobs[i].batch}`, reply: String(r).slice(0, 200) }))
